9:T863,The method has two main components. The first derives Muon’s update direction from a constrained response model. The weight update is posed as a response of the parameter matrix to an applied force, with an output-side safety budget limiting how much the update may perturb the model’s outputs. Among all admissible responses, the preferred one is the maximally dissipative direction. Under the paper’s assumptions, this leads to the orthogonal polar factor of the momentum matrix, which is exactly the semi-orthogonalized direction used by Muon. This is a matrix-level geometric argument, not a coordinate-wise adaptive scaling argument. That is the key distinction from AdamW: AdamW relies on per-parameter second-moment preconditioning, while Muon chooses an update shape that is better behaved in spectral terms and less dominated by a few singular directions.

The second component derives a two-timescale momentum from stress relaxation. Standard momentum assumes a single exponential decay, which corresponds to a single relaxation mode. The paper argues that this is too crude for real training dynamics. Borrowing from Maxwell-type viscoelastic models, it decomposes internal stress into a fast and a slow component, each tracked by its own EMA coefficient, and combines them into the momentum that is later semi-orthogonalized. This yields the Bi-Maxwell optimizer. Importantly, the rest of Muon is kept unchanged: the orthogonalization step stays, and the benchmark recipe is otherwise held fixed. That makes the causal claim cleaner, because the observed gains can be attributed mainly to the memory structure rather than to a bundle of recipe changes.

A central conceptual point is that the optimal memory length should not be constant over training. Early on, gradient directions change quickly, so long memory mixes in stale directions and hurts responsiveness. Later, directions evolve more slowly, so longer memory improves denoising and accumulates consistent signal. Bi-Maxwell does not explicitly schedule beta over time; instead, it uses two fixed timescales to approximate a training-dependent effective memory length.a:T773,The headline result is on the public modded-nanogpt optimizer speedrun benchmark. Replacing Muon’s single-timescale momentum with the Bi-Maxwell memory reaches the target loss at step 2635, improving on the standing public record of 2690 steps at the time. The paper also reports a 40-step improvement over a bare tuned-Muon baseline without extra add-ons such as SOAP. The absolute gain is modest, but on a benchmark that has already been heavily tuned by the community, a further improvement from changing only the momentum structure is meaningful.

The second important result is a read-only measurement study over 8 independent training trajectories, aimed at estimating the optimal momentum memory length during training. The measured trend matches the theory: the preferred memory is shorter early in training and becomes longer later. The value of this experiment is less about the exact numbers and more about turning a usually opaque hyperparameter into something that can be observed and discussed over the course of optimization.

The paper also makes a point about evaluation discipline. The comparison is not against a weak in-house baseline, but against a public standing record on a benchmark that has been tuned adversarially over time. Since the rest of Muon is held fixed and only the memory mechanism is changed, the attribution is tighter than in many optimizer papers where gains can be confounded by recipe drift.

At least from the provided full text, the direct empirical validation is still centered on the public small-scale speedrun setup. The paper cites prior evidence that Muon itself has scaled to billion-parameter and trillion-token settings, but the new Bi-Maxwell variant is not yet shown in a full large-scale pretraining run here. So the empirical status is best read as theory-driven validation on a strong public benchmark, not yet a finalized frontier-scale recipe.b:T68d,Start with the Introduction to understand the framing: the paper is not merely rebranding momentum, but assigning distinct physical meanings to update direction and memory. Then focus on Section 3, especially the part around stress relaxation and memory length. That is where the paper’s real novelty sits. While reading, keep two questions in mind. First, what exactly is constrained by the output-side safety budget, and why does that lead to the polar-factor or semi-orthogonalized direction? Second, why is a single EMA equivalent to an overly restrictive single-mode relaxation assumption, and why is a two-timescale model the minimal useful extension?

In the experiments, prioritize the main benchmark result and the plots measuring optimal memory length over training. The former answers whether the method helps; the latter answers whether the theory is reflected in data. If time is limited, it is fine to postpone judging every physical analogy literally and instead inspect which assumptions are essential for the derivation and which are mainly there to obtain a tractable form. The appendix discussion on assumption boundaries and relaxations is worth reading because it determines how far this framework might generalize beyond the exact setting studied here.

Two follow-up questions are especially worth carrying into a deeper read. One is whether Bi-Maxwell should be extended to richer relaxation spectra, possibly continuous or layer-specific. The other is whether the optimal memory length could be estimated online and used to adapt beta directly, instead of approximating it with two fixed EMAs. The paper opens both directions but does not close them.c:T6cb,The proposed method is Adaptive Log-Space (AL) quantization, embedded in a broader analysis of optimizer-state heterogeneity. The authors first observe that many non-negative optimizer states, especially second moments and confidence accumulators, are heavy-tailed, vary in dynamic range across blocks, and often contain exact zeros. Standard blockwise linear quantization can collapse small positive values to zero, which destroys the distinction between dormant state and weak but nonzero history. AL addresses this by fitting a logarithmic interval to the positive values within each block while reserving code zero exclusively for exact zero, yielding the invariant q = 0 if and only if x = 0. This preserves true zeros and prevents positive second moments from being quantized away into zero. The design is not a single uniform low-bit policy. Non-negative states can use AL8 or AL16, signed momentum is encoded separately, and CAME confidence states may use higher precision than second moments. A second key idea is topology-aware grouping. The paper shows that quantization blocks should align with the optimizer’s state topology: cutting across Adafactor row/column factors or mixing unrelated statistics in one block can amplify update error. The study covers four optimizer paths—dense AdamW, factored Adafactor, confidence-guided CAME, and projected-state APOLLO—and evaluates not only state reconstruction but also update-domain fidelity, temporal drift, and error propagation through inverse square roots, factor reconstruction, confidence modulation, and projected scaling. The implementation includes both a Python reference path and fused CUDA kernels, with separate checks for algorithmic and numerical consistency.d:T5a3,The experiments are organized into controlled diagnostics and end-to-end pretraining runs. In the diagnostic part, the authors trace optimizer states from language-model pretraining and compare their value ranges, exact-zero patterns, and temporal behavior. They then evaluate how different quantization schemes affect both state reconstruction and update error. The conclusions are deliberately nuanced rather than universal. For dense AdamW, AL8 is competitive with the evaluated 8-bit AdamW baseline. For CAME, confidence states are more precision-sensitive than second moments, so using too low a precision there hurts update fidelity more noticeably. For Adafactor, protecting sensitive tensors and matching quantization granularity to row/column factor topology is materially better than coarse uniform blocking. For APOLLO, projected-space states exhibit yet another error-propagation pattern, reinforcing the point that they should not be treated as ordinary dense arrays. The end-to-end validation uses 20K-step TinyLlama-1.1B pretraining and 100K-step GPT-2 pretraining. The paper’s overall conclusion is bounded: AL8 can match existing 8-bit baselines on several paths, but a single low-precision recipe is not sufficient for all structured optimizer states. The available text does not expose the full final-loss tables, so the most useful takeaway is the pattern of sensitivity and failure modes rather than one headline metric.e:T49b,Start with the introduction and the figure that contrasts the four optimizer-state topologies. That framing is essential; without it, the rest can look like a minor quantization tweak. Then focus on the paper’s three analysis axes: representation, topology, and update semantics. The most informative experiments are the ones that translate state error into update error, because they explain why similar reconstruction quality can still lead to different training outcomes. After that, read the AL representation details, especially the exact-zero invariant and the motivation for log-space coding of non-negative EMA states. In the experiments, prioritize the ablations on block granularity, parameter grouping, and confidence-state precision, then read the TinyLlama-1.1B and GPT-2 pretraining sections. For a quick skim, keep three points: structured optimizer states cannot be handled like dense Adam states, CAME confidence states are a distinct sensitivity point, and quantization groups should respect state topology. A focused read should take around 30–45 minutes; reproducing the work would require a closer look at the implementation and CUDA-validation sections.f:T459,1. **Spectral Probing Analysis**: At checkpoints along real training trajectories, the momentum buffer is decomposed into singular directions, and the loss-optimal step size along each direction is estimated on held-out data. The spectral profile is found to be highly anisotropic and stable: a 'volatile head' at the 'Edge-of-Stability' supports only small step sizes, while a 'tolerant bulk' permits much larger steps.
2. **Unified Perspective**: SGD allocates step size proportional to singular values (opposite to landscape suggestions); Adam's coordinate-wise rescaling mitigates but doesn't solve the mismatch; Muon's whitening to a uniform scale reallocates step mass from the head to the bulk.
3. **SAMuon Algorithm**: To exploit the bulk's capacity for larger steps, Spectral-Aware Muon (SAMuon) is proposed. It imposes a static, head-anchored prior on the whitened update. The full SAMuon fits a log-rank-linear shape via randomized SVD; the simplified SAMuon-lite uses power iteration to pin the head and uniformly amplifies the bulk. Both add no persistent state and negligible computational overhead.10:T49c,The paper formulates validation as a linear inverse problem. The unknown reliability surface is f. Each validation intervention v_j observes an integral <v_j, f>. A deployment choice k asks for <k, f>. The central theorem states that, over all bounded reliability functions 0≤f≤1, the deployment target is exactly identifiable from the validation evidence if and only if k lies in the span of the validation kernels. Otherwise, the exact worst-case ambiguity equals the L1 distance from k to that span, called the blind residual. This is an attainable ambiguity, not merely a loose bound. The paper then treats post-evidence target selection: if the deployment target is chosen after seeing validation results, pointwise intervals are insufficient; validity for arbitrary selectors is equivalent to simultaneous coverage over the whole target family. For iid best-of-N, score percentiles U are uniform and selecting the maximum among N candidates gives the kernel k_N(u)=N u^{N-1}. Auditing best-of-n for n=1,...,m spans polynomials of degree m-1, so certifying a larger N becomes a bounded Hausdorff moment problem over increasingly tail-concentrated order-statistic kernels.11:T48f,Daedalus-150M is a convolution–attention hybrid decoder. Out of 18 blocks, only 6 are full attention; the other 12 are short convolution blocks with kernel length L=3 depthwise conv and a fixed recurrent state of width L-1=2 timesteps, making their per-token decode cost independent of context length. Attention layers are interleaved across depth (a fixed C/A pattern) to preserve long-range retrieval at multiple representation levels. To further reduce cache traffic, attention uses grouped-query attention (12 Q heads, 4 KV heads). The model ties input/output embeddings to cut parameters and memory traffic, and uses a narrower FFN (2048, ~2.67×d_model) to reduce bandwidth-heavy matrices. The paper explicitly documents rejected options (MoE due to export/runtime constraints and lack of sub-1B precedent; position-free attention due to export format; distillation due to teacher-logit storage cost). A first-order CPU decode cost model is provided: per token, read quantized weights once plus KV-cache reads proportional to context length for each attention layer; this yields an analytic cache coefficient κ used to predict hybrid vs dense decoding costs.12:T491,The analysis is set in the continuous-time Markov chain formulation of discrete diffusion. A transition-rate matrix defines the forward noising process and a family of marginal distributions p_t. The reverse process requires concrete scores, i.e. pairwise ratios p_t(y)/p_t(x). SEDD learns these ratios with the score-entropy loss, a weighted Bregman divergence D(a,b)=a/b-1-log(a/b), where the weights are induced by the transition structure.

The main contribution is a minimax treatment of this estimation problem. The paper first derives a lower bound for estimating a single concrete score function under the score-entropy risk. It then constructs a simple estimator, essentially a smoothed or clipped empirical plug-in estimator for the relevant probability ratios, and proves that its risk nearly matches the lower bound. The single-time result is then connected back to SEDD by controlling the time-averaged score-estimation term that appears in KL guarantees for the generated distribution. This complements analyses of tau-leaping, uniformization, Gillespie, or Euler samplers, which study how to simulate the reverse chain once accurate scores are available.13:T4bb,A sampling-based watermark adapted to diffusion decoding.
- Injection: replace position-indexed i.i.d. Gumbel perturbations with a smooth, locally auto-correlated Gumbel field (SAC). The field is constructed via a Gaussian copula so that each coordinate keeps Gumbel marginals (under the paper’s assumptions) while introducing controlled local dependence across neighboring positions.
- Rationale: diffusion decoding refines multiple positions in parallel; independent high-frequency perturbations across neighbors can conflict with local consistency during iterative updates, causing oscillations or incoherence.
- Mechanistic analysis: quantify “latent perturbation roughness” via a local-difference energy and show how positive low-lag dependence reduces this roughness (the paper provides an analytic form contrasting i.i.d. vs SAC).
- Detection: a SAC-aware detector using covariance-aware filtering plus native-sample calibration to manage false positives. A global-offset scan is added as a coarse synchronization recovery tool under mild token–signal misalignment.
Overall, it modifies keyed randomness during DLM decoding and pairs it with a matched detector, rather than changing DLM training.14:T449,The diagnostic pair is a Qwen3.5-27B mentor and a Qwen3.5-4B student. On Multi-IF, linear probes on mentor states show a large freshness gap: stale-state accuracy falls from 0.79 at t=0 to 0.47 at t=512, while fresh-state accuracy stays between 0.76 and 0.80. This drift also affects behavior. Static guidance reduces the 4B student’s constraint satisfaction by 2.5 points below the no-guidance baseline, while refreshing every 16 tokens turns it into a 2.0-point gain over that baseline. Fresh but mismatched memory does not help, which supports the content-freshness explanation. Across 13 datasets, MentorPulse closes 52.2% of the mentor-student gap on the main pair, roughly twice the recovery of the strongest prior alternative. Gains concentrate on long-output tasks. Short outputs often finish before refresh matters, and very large mentor-student capability gaps reduce the margin. The proposed V64 read-distribution indicator helps screen pairs before deployment. Throughput measurements place R=16 among the efficient settings tested against text-to-text guidance on long-output tasks.15:Ta03,技术主线很完整，可以分成诊断、推导、修正三步。

第一步是诊断 solver coupling。作者先写清楚标准 self-conditioning recurrence：每一步模型接收当前 latent z_k、时间 t_k，以及上一时刻 clean prediction 作为 self-conditioning 输入 m_k。训练时，m 是由同一个当前 z 通过一条 stop-gradient 分支得到；推理时，m_k = p_{k-1}，但此时 z_k 已经经过 solver 用 p_{k-1} 更新过。于是同一份信息通过两条路径进入模型：一条隐式地在 latent 里，一条显式地在 self-conditioning 输入里。这个双通道重复在小步长时还不太严重，但 few-step 时每步跨度大，solver 折叠更强，冗余迅速放大。

第二步是把这个失配拆成两个可修正的后果。其一是 self-conditioning redundancy。作者利用冻结模型的投影权重，分析 latent 输入通道和 self-conditioning 输入通道在表示空间中的共享方向。通过对相关矩阵或投影结构做特征分解，识别出两条路径重叠最强的 eigendirections，然后在采样时对 self-conditioning 输入沿这些方向做抑制，让它更多提供 latent 尚未携带的互补信息。这里的关键不是简单缩放整个 self-conditioning，而是按几何方向有选择地 damp 掉冗余分量，所以叫 untied：不再把 solver 中使用的预测和 self-conditioning 中使用的预测视为同一个对象。

其二是 solver approximation gap。标准 solver 在一步开始时只用单点预测 p_k 去近似该步积分所需的平均预测，但真实需要的是区间上的平均量，这个误差是一阶依赖于步长的。作者用 prediction history 去近似这个 step-average prediction，并用离线轨迹统计来定标修正尺度。重要的是，修正后的 prediction 只喂给 solver 做 latent update，而原始 prediction 仍保留给下一步 self-conditioning。这样就把“给 solver 的量”和“给模型自条件的量”解耦了。

第三步是组装成 Untied Self-Conditioning。它是一个 training-free sampler，每步仍只需一次模型前向，不增加 NFE。流程上：模型输出当前 clean prediction；原始预测缓存为下一步 self-conditioning；同时对其做两类修正，一类是基于投影几何的冗余抑制，另一类是基于历史的 solver 平均预测校正；最后用修正后的量更新 latent。这个设计很克制，没有引入额外网络，也没有做 test-time optimization，而是直接利用现有模型结构和采样轨迹信息。16:T97e,The method unfolds in three stages: diagnosis, derivation, and correction.

First, the paper diagnoses solver coupling in the standard self-conditioning recurrence. At step k, the model takes the current latent z_k, time t_k, and a self-conditioning input m_k derived from the previous clean prediction. In training, m is obtained from the same current noisy state through a stop-gradient branch, so there is no solver update between z and m. In sampling, however, m_k = p_{k-1} while z_k has already been updated using p_{k-1}. The same information therefore enters the model twice: implicitly through the latent and explicitly through the self-conditioning input. With small steps this is limited; with few large steps it becomes substantial.

Second, the authors decompose the mismatch into two correctable consequences. The first is self-conditioning redundancy. Using the frozen projection weights of the trained model, they analyze which directions in representation space are shared by the latent-input pathway and the self-conditioning pathway. An eigendecomposition identifies directions where the explicit self-conditioning signal is most redundant with information already embedded in the latent. At inference time, those directions are damped so that the self-conditioning input contributes complementary information rather than repeating what the latent already carries. This is a directional correction, not a global rescaling.

The second consequence is a solver approximation gap. A standard solver uses a single-point prediction at the start of the step to approximate the average prediction needed for the exact integral over that interval. The authors show that this gap is first-order in step width. They then approximate the step-average prediction from prediction history, with the correction scale calibrated using offline trajectory statistics. Crucially, the corrected prediction is used only for the solver update, while the raw prediction is stored as the self-conditioning input for the next step.

These two ideas are combined into Untied Self-Conditioning, a training-free sampler that still uses one model evaluation per step. The prediction used for the solver and the prediction used for self-conditioning are no longer tied to be the same object. The design is restrained: no extra network, no retraining, no additional NFE, only a better use of the model’s own geometry and trajectory history.17:T6d9,The empirical case rests on three kinds of evidence.

First, the headline generation results are strong. On both ELF and LangFlow, Untied Self-Conditioning improves quality at every tested NFE, with the largest gains in the low-step regime. The abstract reports that at 8 model evaluations, LangFlow reduces GenPPL on OpenWebText from 531 to 62, an 8.6x improvement, and on ELF-B from 71 to 43. At 32 evaluations on ELF-B, it reaches GenPPL 21, approaching the data reference, while retaining 95% throughput. These numbers matter because they show better quality at essentially the same compute budget.

Second, the paper includes a controlled coupling experiment. It varies only the dependence between successive steps while keeping each step’s marginal prediction distribution fixed. As coupling increases, the benefit of self-conditioning shrinks monotonically, and under strong coupling full self-conditioning becomes harmful. This is one of the most convincing parts of the paper because it isolates the mechanism: the issue is not simply that single-step predictions become worse in few-step sampling, but that solver-induced cross-step coupling makes the explicit self-conditioning pathway redundant or counterproductive.

Third, the ablations separate the two corrections: redundancy damping and solver-average correction. Both help, and their effects compound in the few-step regime. One mainly improves the quality of the self-conditioning signal; the other improves the numerical update used by the solver. The paper also emphasizes that the gains do not come from extra forward passes. When reading the experiments closely, the most informative pieces are the NFE-quality curves, the controlled coupling plots, and the component ablations.18:T547,This one deserves a close read. Start with Section 2 to make sure the standard self-conditioning recurrence and the train–inference discrepancy are fully clear. Then spend most of the time on Section 3, which is the core of the paper: it derives the redundancy problem and the solver approximation gap separately. If that section is understood, the main contribution is understood. Section 4 is shorter and mainly assembles the final sampler. In Section 5, focus on three parts: the few-step headline results, the controlled coupling experiment, and the component ablations. The most important figures are the mismatch schematic, the projection/eigendirection analysis, and the GenPPL-versus-NFE curves.

Three follow-up questions are worth keeping in mind. First, the geometric correction based on frozen projection weights may generalize to other diffusion or flow language models, and perhaps even to test-time corrections in AR models. Second, the solver correction uses offline trajectory statistics, which raises the question of how model- or sampler-specific the calibration is and whether it can be made adaptive. Third, although the method is inference-time only, it exposes a training deficiency: if training explicitly simulated solver-induced coupling, would the model learn a more robust self-conditioning representation from the start?19:T4dd,The authors define an exact conditional-marginal oracle model to isolate parallelization error from model approximation error. A deterministic adaptive policy chooses the next reveal set from the observed partial assignment. The selected variables are then sampled independently using their true conditional marginals rather than from their true joint conditional. Approximation error is measured by forward KL, which has a chain-rule decomposition aligned with the reveal process and corresponds to excess expected log loss. Serial depth is the minimum target-averaged number of rounds needed to meet a KL budget. The central proof aligns each round's KL contribution with the conditional total correlation of the variables revealed in that round. The identity applies to random and history-dependent reveal sets. The paper then turns the identity into upper and lower bounds for structured families: logarithmic exact sampling for Bernoulli walks via hierarchical bisection, logarithmic-in-length zero-error schedules for finite-order Markov chains with a factor depending on Markov order, linear expected depth for uniform random permutations at fixed error, and several binary-alphabet constructions with polylogarithmic to polynomial depth.1a:T53b,The theoretical results give the main evidence. For the Bernoulli walk, hierarchical bisection achieves exact sampling in logarithmically many rounds, while contiguous left-to-right schedules require linearly many rounds to maintain fixed accuracy. For uniform random permutations, every fixed-error policy needs a linear number of expected rounds; under a hard round cap, the optimal error reduces exactly to an integer-composition problem, yielding fixed-round asymptotics, a finite-blocklength pairs-first phase, and a joint scaling frontier. Over a binary alphabet, uniform balanced binary strings have depth on the order of squared log sequence length at any fixed positive error, while independent one-hot blocks give matching square-root-depth lower bounds against arbitrary deterministic value-adaptive policies. Rectangular block constructions realize polynomial exponents up to one half. The empirical section is diagnostic: it evaluates generic schedules and deployed decoding rules on 542 sequences from WikiText and model-generated text across four domains using a single 0.5B model and one sampling temperature. A paired self-sampling study on 231 held-out prompts compares teacher-forced pseudo-costs with output quality under an external autoregressive evaluator, and also tests a model-independent spaced-profile schedule.1b:T820,方法延续 FlashPrefill 的两阶段思路。先做 block-level 的粗粒度打分，再只对被选中的 block 做精细 attention。原始 FlashPrefill 用 probe queries 和 block mean-pooled key 来估计每个 key block 的重要性，并用基于峰值分数的动态阈值替代 Top-k/Top-p 排序，从而避免全局排序开销。它还保留 sink blocks、局部滑窗和最近块，以兼顾因果约束和常见注意力模式。

V2 的第一个关键改动是 mean correction term。原方法在极端稀疏时直接截断未选 block 的 softmax 分母和分子，忽略掉被剪枝块的质量，误差会迅速放大。V2 为每个 key block 预先计算 pooled K/V 统计量，用零阶近似去补偿被丢弃块对 softmax mass 和 value aggregation 的贡献。直观上，它不再把未选 block 当成完全不存在，而是用块均值代表其剩余贡献。这样做的好处是代价低，不需要恢复 token-level 计算，但能显著缓和高 sparsity 下的偏差。

第二个关键改动是 kernel 重写，目标是对齐 Hopper 时代的高性能 dense attention 实现。文中提到三点：PackGQA memory access、warp specialization、pingpong pipelining。前者针对 grouped-query attention 的访存组织，减少无效带宽和访存碎片；warp specialization 把不同 warp 分配给不同职责，提高流水并行；pingpong pipeline 则利用 Hopper 上的异步搬运和计算重叠机制，把数据准备和计算交替推进。作者明确说 V2 是按 FlashAttention-3/4 的实现思路重构，而不是停留在 FA2 时代的 kernel 结构上。

第三个关键改动是系统兼容性。V2 原生支持 paged KV cache 和 continuous batching，并集成到 SGLang 这类现代推理框架中。这个点很重要，因为很多 academic sparse attention 方法默认 contiguous KV layout，离真实 serving 很远；一旦接入 paged cache，索引、页表、batch 动态拼接都会改变 kernel 设计。V2 把这一层一起处理了，所以论文不只是算子 benchmark，而是端到端 TTFT 改善。1c:T8b0,FlashPrefill V2 keeps the two-stage structure of FlashPrefill. It first performs block-level coarse scoring, then computes fine-grained attention only on selected blocks. The original method uses probe queries and mean-pooled keys to estimate block salience, and replaces Top-k/Top-p sorting with a max-based dynamic threshold. It also preserves sink blocks, a local sliding window, and recent blocks to respect causal structure and common attention patterns.

The first major addition in V2 is a mean correction term. In the original truncation-based approximation, unselected blocks are simply dropped from both the softmax denominator and numerator. Under extreme sparsity, that discarded probability mass becomes too large to ignore. V2 compensates for pruned blocks using precomputed pooled K/V statistics for each block, effectively adding back a zero-order surrogate contribution. Intuitively, the method no longer treats pruned blocks as nonexistent; it represents their residual effect through block means. This keeps the correction cheap while significantly reducing approximation error at high sparsity.

The second major change is a Hopper-oriented kernel redesign. The paper highlights PackGQA memory access, warp specialization, and pingpong pipelining. PackGQA improves memory organization for grouped-query attention and reduces bandwidth waste. Warp specialization assigns different roles to different warps to improve overlap and utilization. Pingpong pipelining exploits Hopper-style asynchronous data movement and compute overlap. The authors explicitly position V2 as aligned with FlashAttention-3/4 implementation principles rather than older FA2-style kernels.

The third change is systems compatibility. V2 natively supports paged KV cache and continuous batching, and is integrated into SGLang-like serving frameworks. This is important because many academic sparse-attention methods assume contiguous KV layouts and do not survive contact with real serving systems. Once paged cache, page tables, and dynamic batching enter the picture, the kernel design changes materially. V2 addresses that layer directly, so the contribution is not just an operator benchmark but an end-to-end TTFT improvement.1d:T620,The empirical story has three parts: speed, quality, and deployability. On NVIDIA H20 at 128K context in BF16, FlashPrefill V2 reports up to 27.19x speedup over FlashAttention-2 during prefill. Its FP8 variant reaches 47.26x. More importantly, even against a much stronger dense baseline aligned with FlashAttention-3/4, it still achieves 17.54x speedup in BF16 and 30.49x in FP8. That means the gain is not an artifact of comparing against an outdated dense kernel. The paper also notes that acceleration remains visible even at 4K sequence length, suggesting that sparse selection and launch overheads are kept low enough to matter outside only ultra-long contexts.

At the system level, after integration into SGLang, the method reduces end-to-end time-to-first-token by up to 4.8x at 128K with only marginal accuracy loss. This result is more convincing than raw kernel throughput because it includes the effects of paged KV cache, continuous batching, and framework-level scheduling.

On accuracy, the headline claim is that mean correction keeps degradation manageable even under extreme sparsity. The method section explains why: naive truncation drops the softmax mass of pruned blocks, while the correction restores an approximation of that contribution using block-level statistics. The excerpt provided here does not include the full downstream quality tables or exact error curves, but the intended contribution is clear: not zero-loss sparsification, but a much better quality-speed tradeoff in the high-sparsity regime where deployment actually benefits.1e:T4d8,Read this paper with a systems lens. Start from the introduction and keep the three prototype gaps in mind: approximation quality, kernel efficiency, and serving compatibility. Then go straight to the mean-correction section and understand why it restores pruned softmax mass. You do not need to follow every algebraic detail, but you should recognize that this is a cheap zero-order block-level correction rather than a heavier higher-order scheme. After that, read the kernel-design section carefully, especially how it maps to Hopper execution behavior and why PackGQA, warp specialization, and pingpong pipelining appear together. Finally, spend time on the integration and end-to-end results, not only the operator microbenchmarks.

If you work on long-context serving, the most useful figures are the speed curves across context lengths, precisions, and baselines, plus the accuracy-versus-sparsity tradeoff. If your focus is more on pretraining, the main takeaway is simpler: many long-context ideas look good at the algorithm level, but deployable context scaling often depends on whether the kernel and serving interface are co-designed. A solid skim should take 30–45 minutes; a reproduction-oriented read will take much longer.1f:T655,FleetSieve treats profiling as downstream decision identification. For each workload-class/configuration cell, it maintains intervals for sustainable capacity and tail latency rather than a single estimate. It then solves two fleet allocations under the same resource constraints and lexicographic objective: a conservative allocation using lower capacity and upper tail bounds, and an optimistic allocation using upper capacity and lower tail bounds. The objective first enforces minimum fulfillment floors for critical classes when feasible, then maximizes the minimum satisfaction ratio, then total served goodput, and finally reduces fragmentation.

The key idea is the acquisition rule. FleetSieve does not measure the cell with the largest uncertainty, nor does it try to cover the grid uniformly. It measures the configuration expected to reduce disagreement between the conservative and optimistic downstream allocations. In other words, a cell with high uncertainty is not important if no plausible outcome would change the fleet decision. Conversely, a cell becomes important if resolving it could flip SLO feasibility or alter resource allocation for a critical workload.

The paper also introduces a conditional decision certificate with three states: Certified-Feasible, Undecided, and Certified-Infeasible. The wording is careful. The certificate is not distribution-free or unconditional; it is valid only under the empirical uncertainty model used to bound the unknown performance table. That restraint is a good sign: the method is presented as an engineering decision tool, not as a universal guarantee.20:T491,The evaluation is intentionally narrow and concrete: one 31B open-weight decoder model, one H100 node, FP8, a vLLM-based serving stack, speculative decoding disabled, and candidate TP degrees {2, 4, 8}. Each profiling cell is measured for 300 seconds. The main metric is how many profiling GPU-seconds are needed to recover the oracle aggregate fleet decision.

The headline result is modest but real: on the fixed H100 measurement grid, FleetSieve reaches the oracle aggregate decision with 22,200 GPU-seconds, a 6.9% reduction relative to uniform profiling. The paper is refreshingly explicit that gains are selective rather than universal: the reduction is larger for Chat and absent for Code. That matters because it clarifies when the method helps. If unresolved cells can still change the global allocation, decision-aware profiling is useful. If the allocation is effectively determined early, the extra machinery may not buy much. The experiments also show why joint modeling of capacity and tail latency is necessary: throughput-only profiling can certify configurations that look efficient but violate the actual SLO, which then corrupts fleet-level planning.21:T584,CacheRoute builds a periodically refreshed routing table that plans prefix affinity and expected load together, prioritizing cache stability over per-request reactive remapping.
- Inputs/abstraction: per-key arrival rates λ_b for business keys; R routable destinations (a destination is a model-server group; in the 70B setup, TP=2).
- Admission (warm set): admit the highest-rate keys into an affinity-managed warm set under a warm-prefix slot budget; non-admitted traffic falls back to cache-blind power-of-two choices.
- Load cap via replication: calibrate q_cap from a single destination’s latency/load knee. For each key, allocate enough destinations so the expected per-destination load contributed by that key is ≤ q_cap. Replication is primarily for load control (capping per-destination contribution), not for improving hit rate per se.
- Placement: assign admitted keys (and their replica counts) to destinations using LPT (longest-processing-time-first) list scheduling to reduce expected load imbalance.
- Control interval: keep the table fixed for a period to preserve cache warmth; avoid reactive spilling that would send the next request to a cold destination once a cap binds.
The novelty is not LPT or top-k admission individually, but the combined routing design and the empirical characterization of when planned affinity beats both cache-blind balancing and reactive cache-aware routing.22:T7ab,方法分成两部分：TDES 和 SABA。

TDES（Target-Distilled Edge Scoring）解决父子错配。现有 DDTree 的边选择近似是 parent-agnostic 的：child token 在不同 parent 下贡献相同，只由该位置的 token probability 决定。GRAFT 改成显式给 edge 打分。做法是从 target model 的验证轨迹里蒸馏一个轻量 edge scorer，输入是相邻位置候选节点及其上下文特征，输出该 parent-child transition 被 target 接受的兼容性分数。然后树构建时不再只按各位置 token 概率乘积选路径，而是结合 edge score 进行 parent-conditional 组装。这样保留了 DLM 一次前向产出候选节点的优点，又补上了“节点之间是否能连成 target 偏好的路径”这一层信息。

从机制上看，这一步很像把 target 的局部条件分布偏好压缩成一个便宜的结构预测器。它不是重新跑 target，也不是让 drafter 变成 AR，而是在 assembly 阶段补一个 learned compatibility model。相比直接增大候选集，这种做法更有效，因为问题不是候选 token 不在，而是树结构把它们接错了。

SABA（State-Aware Budget Allocation）解决固定预算失配。作者把每轮 throughput 看成 accepted gain 与 verification overhead 的函数，学习一个按当前 decoding state 选择 tree budget 的策略。直觉上，easy round 本来 acceptance 就长，再加节点收益很快饱和；hard round 适度扩树更值钱，但也不是越大越好。SABA 用当前轮的状态特征预测不同 budget 下的收益，选 throughput 最优预算。这里的关键不是复杂控制器，而是把“树大小”从静态超参变成在线决策变量。

整体上，GRAFT 没有改 DLM 本身，也没有改 target verification 机制，而是专门优化 DLM-based tree assembly 这一层。这种切分是合理的，因为瓶颈正出在 one-pass future distributions 到 executable tree 的映射。23:T781,GRAFT has two components: TDES and SABA.

TDES, or Target-Distilled Edge Scoring, addresses parent-child mismatch. DDTree is effectively parent-agnostic: a child token contributes the same score regardless of which parent path it extends, because scoring is driven by per-position token probabilities. GRAFT instead learns an explicit edge scorer distilled from target-model traces. The scorer takes candidate parent-child pairs from adjacent positions, together with contextual features, and predicts how compatible that transition is with the target model. Tree assembly then uses these edge scores, rather than only the product of marginal token probabilities, to select target-compatible paths under a node budget.

Mechanistically, this is a lightweight structural predictor that compresses local target preferences into a cheap model. It does not rerun the target and does not force the DLM drafter into autoregressive expansion. It patches the missing conditional dependency at the tree-assembly stage. That is the right intervention point, because the failure mode is not merely missing candidate tokens; it is incorrect attachment among already available candidates.

SABA, or State-Aware Budget Allocation, addresses budget misallocation. The paper models per-round throughput as a trade-off between draft gain and verification cost, then chooses the budget conditioned on the current decoding state. Easy rounds already have long accepted prefixes, so larger trees mostly add cost. Hard rounds benefit more from extra nodes, but only up to a saturation point. SABA predicts the utility of different budgets from state features and selects the throughput-optimal one online.

Overall, GRAFT leaves the DLM and the target verification mechanism unchanged. It focuses specifically on the mapping from one-pass future distributions to an executable draft tree. That decomposition is sensible and technically clean.24:T4a2,The main empirical claim is consistent end-to-end throughput improvement with very small overhead. The paper reports 2.13x to 6.36x throughput gains over baselines across models and datasets, while adding less than 0.5 ms overhead per decoding round. That matters because it suggests the method is not trading away the cost structure of speculative decoding.

The ablations are more informative than the headline numbers. TDES improves MAT, indicating that parent-child compatibility is a real bottleneck for DLM-based tree construction. The paper shows both examples and aggregate evidence that target-compatible tokens are often already present among candidates, but become unusable because they are connected to the wrong parent. SABA shows that a fixed budget is not robust: the throughput-optimal tree size varies substantially across rounds. Dynamic allocation preserves most of the acceptance gain while avoiding unnecessary verification cost.

From a systems perspective, the strongest result is not a single benchmark number but the combination of stable gains across tasks and low added latency. That makes the method more credible as a practical layer on top of DLM drafters.25:T455,This is a skim paper, but the introduction, method section, and ablations are worth reading carefully.

Focus on three things. First, the two failure modes defined in the introduction: parent-child mismatch and budget misallocation. If those are convincing, the rest of the paper follows naturally. Second, inspect how TDES gets supervision from target traces and what features the edge scorer actually uses. The important question is what information is added beyond marginal token probabilities. Third, check whether SABA is optimizing throughput directly or only a proxy such as acceptance length.

For figures and tables, prioritize the mismatch examples, the MAT/throughput comparisons, and the curves showing diminishing returns with larger budgets. Expected reading time is about 25 to 35 minutes. If reading selectively, the problem setup, the two modules, and the ablations are enough. If reading more deeply, two follow-up questions are worth keeping in mind: how target-specific the distilled edge scorer is, and whether the budget policy can generalize to broader adaptive verification strategies.26:T4ff,The method, DPQ (Doubt-Preserving Quantization), is a family of pre-quantization calibration-data recipes rather than a new quantizer. The pipeline is lightweight. First, run the full-precision model on candidate examples. Then select target-aware 'fragile' examples using FP uncertainty signals. Two signal families matter most: high-doubt examples, such as high entropy, low confidence, or small top-2 margin; and answerability-boundary examples, especially for answer/no-answer settings like SQuAD2. These are mixed with generic anchor examples and then passed to an unchanged quantizer such as GPTQ or AWQ. The theoretical argument is modest but useful: if the deployment target puts more mass near decision boundaries, while the calibration mixture is dominated by generic anchors, the optimal calibration set will differ from the one preferred by broad MCQA-style targets. The paper calls this mixture mismatch. The framing is built around two preservation risks: a distributional risk that measures deviation between quantized and FP predictive distributions, and a boundary risk that measures decision flips in low-margin regions, optionally reweighted toward answerability or abstention-heavy inputs. This is a better fit for real systems than accuracy-only calibration.27:T539,The evaluation spans 8 language models, 9 NLP benchmarks, and 22 comparison methods or configurations. The metric suite is broader than standard quantization papers: besides ECE, adaptive ECE, NLL, and Brier score, the authors report FP-behavior metrics such as FP agreement, JSD between quantized and FP predictive distributions, confidence shift, top-two margin drift, and margin correlation. On SQuAD2 they also evaluate answerability-boundary behavior directly. Three findings stand out. First, the best calibration recipe depends strongly on the target. For boundary-sensitive answerability preservation, a high-boundary mixture such as DPQ-s128-r75 works best. For broad MCQA, milder recipes such as DPQ-r50 or single-signal confidence-only / entropy-only selection are often better. Second, accuracy can hide substantial uncertainty drift: some settings preserve top-1 behavior while materially changing confidence and margin structure. Third, preservation signals transfer only partially across quantizers. The post-hoc calibration and AWQ analyses suggest that some useful signals are not tied to one quantizer, but the best score-preservation recipe still remains quantizer-specific. The paper is less about one headline average gain and more about establishing the robustness of this target dependence across models and tasks.28:T758,系统结果是全文最硬的部分。作者在 NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU 上报告，优化后的 BF16 实现从 4K 上下文开始超过 dense attention；在 32K 时，单层 attention 达到 10.91× speedup。更重要的是，真实的八层 retrofit 在 warm 32K whole-model TTFT 上带来 15.3% 的下降。这个数字没有单层 10× 那么夸张，但更可信，因为它把 attention 之外的层、调度、kernel launch、planning 等开销都算进去了。

训练结果方面，论文做了三种 matched Stage A 对照：Dense continued training、equal-pair-count local sliding、equal-pair-count static-random nonlocal graph。BF1 在三次训练 seed 下都排第一。这里最关键的不是“第一”这个标签，而是控制做得比较细：local sliding 和 random graph 都匹配了 pair budget，因此 BF1 的优势更可能来自拓扑结构，而不是单纯看得更多。换句话说，作者试图回答的是“在相同稀疏预算下，dyadic + first-block 这种图是否比局部或随机图更适合 next-token LM”。

论文还单独讨论了 selected-page decode semantics，并指出在低 batch 场景下，主瓶颈不是 selected-page attention arithmetic，而是 planning lifecycle。这个观察很重要，因为它解释了为什么很多稀疏 decode 方案在 paper benchmark 上很快，落到真实 serving 却收益有限：算子省下来的时间被 page selection、mask planning、runtime orchestration 吃掉了。

从当前给出的正文片段看，底座是 Qwen3-0.6B 几何配置。若全文有 perplexity 或 downstream LM 指标，阅读时要重点看 BF1 retrofit 后相对 dense-continued-training 的差距是否稳定很小，以及这种差距是否随上下文长度扩大。如果长上下文收益建立在明显牺牲短上下文 LM 质量之上，那方法的适用面会窄很多。29:T723,BF1 is a deterministic, block-aligned causal sparse-attention pattern. The sequence is partitioned into blocks of width b, with the reported public configuration using b = 64. For a query block j, the route includes four components: the causal self block, two exact local predecessor blocks, the first global block, and historical predecessor blocks at dyadic distances, i.e. j - 2^r starting from an offset of four blocks. In short, it is local + global-first + dyadic history.

The paper is explicit that this route is related to earlier log-sparse and dilated designs such as LogSparse Transformer and LongNet. The claimed novelty lies elsewhere: pretrained-model retrofit, matched topology-control experiments, and correctness-gated Blackwell measurements. The correctness-gated part is important. The authors do not only benchmark a fast path; they verify partial blocks, backward gradients, dense-path equivalence, future-token isolation, and opposite-order benchmarks up to 32K, which makes the systems claims more credible.

With fixed block width, each converted layer uses O(n log n) selected token interactions and has O(log n) graph communication depth. The communication-depth argument is the structural reason BF1 should beat pure local sliding windows: long-range information can propagate in logarithmically many sparse hops rather than linearly many local layers. Compared with static random nonlocal graphs, BF1 is deterministic and easier to optimize at the kernel level.

Another sensible design choice is that the paper does not replace all attention layers in the model and call it done. It reports an actual eight-layer retrofit separately from an all-layer timing-only ceiling. That makes the results more realistic for pretrained models, where replacing every layer with a sparse operator can be risky.2a:T74e,The strongest evidence is on the systems side. On an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU, the optimized BF16 implementation reportedly crosses dense attention around 4K context length. At 32K, the per-layer attention operator reaches 10.91× speedup. More importantly, the actual eight-layer retrofit reduces warm whole-model TTFT by 15.3% at 32K. That number is much smaller than the per-layer speedup, but it is also much more informative because it includes the rest of the model and runtime overheads.

For language modeling, the paper runs three matched Stage A training comparisons: dense continued training, equal-pair-count local sliding, and equal-pair-count static-random nonlocal graphs. BF1 ranks first in all three matched runs. The key point is not the ranking alone. The controls are designed to keep the sparse budget comparable, so the advantage is more plausibly due to topology rather than simply attending to more pairs. In other words, the paper tries to answer whether a dyadic-plus-first-block graph is a better sparse inductive bias for next-token LM than local-only or random sparse graphs under similar budget.

The decode analysis is also useful. The paper reports selected-page decode semantics and argues that, at low batch, the dominant unresolved cost is planning lifecycle rather than selected-page attention arithmetic. That observation explains why sparse decode methods often look strong in operator benchmarks but deliver limited gains in real serving stacks.

From the provided text, the tested geometry is based on Qwen3-0.6B. When reading the full paper, the most important thing to check is how much LM quality is lost relative to dense continued training, and whether that gap stays small across context lengths. If long-context efficiency comes with a noticeable short-context LM penalty, the deployment envelope becomes narrower.2b:T43b,A good skim order is: operator definition, systems measurements, then matched training controls. Start with the route definition and complexity proposition to understand exactly which blocks are connected and why the selected interactions are O(n log n) with O(log n) communication depth. Then jump to the systems section and focus on the dense crossover point, the 32K per-layer speedup, and the whole-model TTFT for the eight-layer retrofit. Finally, read the matched Stage A training results to see whether topology, sparse budget, and training adaptation are properly disentangled.

If you only have about 25 minutes, prioritize Figure 1, the complexity statement, the correctness-gated Blackwell benchmark tables, and the matched-control training results. Three details are worth deeper inspection: why the first block is used as the global anchor instead of learned global tokens, which eight layers were retrofitted and why, and how the planning-lifecycle overhead is broken down during decode. That last point may be more operationally important than the sparse route itself.2c:T885,方法核心是 trace → execution graph → workload synthesis → deterministic replay → profiling 这一整条链路。

1. 通用 tracing。XPerf 支持对 LangChain、LangGraph 等常见 agent 框架做无侵入或低侵入埋点；对自建 agent 只需很少注释。它记录的不只是 LLM 请求本身，还包括工具调用及其时间信息。

2. 执行图重建。论文用基于 time-span tree 的分析方法，从 traces 中恢复 LLM call、tool call 及其依赖关系，得到 execution graph。这个设计比简单按时间顺序回放更合理，因为 agent 负载里存在并发、等待工具返回、条件分支等结构，只有显式依赖图才能保留真实调度约束。

3. 工作负载合成。作者没有把 benchmark 限定为“原样回放历史 trace”，而是允许在 execution graph 之上改变请求到达模式，构造 online serving、offline batch inference、fixed-concurrency 等不同场景。这一点很关键，因为系统研究需要控制 arrival process，才能比较调度器、batching、cache 策略在不同负载区间的行为。

4. 可复现回放。为保证 replay fidelity，XPerf 对每个 LLM call 提交记录下来的精确 input token IDs，而不是重新 tokenize 文本；这样可以保留 prefix cache 命中行为。必要时还可以强制 serving engine 解码记录过的 output tokens，避免因为模型输出偏移而改变后续控制流。回放时还遵守 execution graph 的依赖顺序，并把工具调用时长纳入时间轴，因此即便被测 serving engine 与 tracing 时不同，负载形态仍尽量贴近原始应用。

5. 细粒度 profiling。系统层面报告 KV cache usage、prefix cache hit rate、token throughput 等；硬件层面报告 GPU tensor core 利用率、memory bandwidth 利用率等。作者强调 profiler 开销很低，避免 benchmark 本身扭曲结果。

和已有工作相比，区别主要在两点：一是它不是只测独立请求，也不是只做 agent 任务完成率；二是它公开、可扩展，并且把“非确定性 agent 行为”通过 trace replay 固定下来，而不是接受 run-to-run variance 作为噪声。2d:T896,The method is a full pipeline: trace collection, execution-graph reconstruction, workload synthesis, deterministic replay, and low-overhead profiling.

1. Application-agnostic tracing. XPerf instruments popular agent frameworks such as LangChain and LangGraph with minimal friction, and supports lightweight annotations for custom agents. It records both LLM calls and tool calls, including timing information.

2. Execution-graph construction. Rather than replaying requests as a flat sequence, XPerf reconstructs dependencies among LLM calls and tool invocations using a time-span-tree-based analysis. This matters because agent workloads contain waiting, branching, and sometimes parallel structure. A dependency graph preserves the scheduling constraints that actually shape serving behavior.

3. Workload synthesis. XPerf does not stop at replaying historical traces. It can alter request arrival patterns over the reconstructed execution graphs to emulate online serving, offline batch inference, and fixed-concurrency settings. This makes the framework useful for controlled systems studies, where arrival processes must be varied independently of application logic.

4. Reproducible replay. For each LLM call, XPerf submits the exact recorded input token IDs, not just the raw text, so prefix-cache behavior is preserved. It can also force the serving engine to decode the recorded output tokens, preventing output drift from changing downstream control flow. Replay respects dependency order in the execution graph and accounts for tool-call durations, so the workload remains realistic even when the target serving engine differs from the one used during trace collection.

5. Fine-grained profiling. XPerf reports serving metrics such as KV-cache usage, prefix-cache hit rate, and token throughput, and hardware metrics such as tensor-core utilization and memory-bandwidth utilization. The profiler is designed to add negligible overhead.

Relative to prior work, the distinction is clear: it is neither an agent-quality benchmark nor a standard serving microbenchmark. Its central idea is to freeze the stochastic control flow of agent applications into a reproducible systems workload.2e:T5aa,The evaluation uses eight agentic applications spanning deep research, coding, Q&A, and general-purpose assistance. The most important results fall into three buckets.

First, replay fidelity. XPerf achieves below 3% mean absolute percentage error in end-to-end request latency for both isolated and concurrent requests. That is the key validation result: if replay were not faithful, the rest of the benchmark would be hard to trust.

Second, workload variance in native agent runs. The paper quantifies how unstable agent execution can be without replay. The headline example is the roughly 70% average variation in the number of LLM calls for the same request under mini-SWE-agent with gpt-oss-120b. This result justifies the entire benchmark design.

Third, bottleneck diagnosis. With replay fixed, XPerf can decompose end-to-end latency and relate it to prefix-cache hits, KV-cache occupancy, token throughput, and GPU compute or bandwidth utilization. The paper’s emphasis is not on claiming one serving engine wins universally, but on showing that the framework can localize where performance is lost under agent-style traffic.

For a foundation-model audience, the useful takeaway is that agent workloads materially change prefix reuse, request-length distributions, and concurrency structure. Optimizations that look effective on standard chat-style benchmarks may behave differently once execution graphs become deeper and more irregular.2f:T46f,The conceptual move is to extend JND from human perception to machine receivers. Instead of asking whether a compressed signal is visually indistinguishable, the paper asks whether the downstream policy response remains effectively unchanged. In a VLA setting, the receiver is a language-conditioned robotic policy and the response is a continuous action vector, including translation, rotation, and gripper control. Compression decisions are therefore guided by action sensitivity rather than by visual similarity or attention mass. Based on the introduction, the method likely defines an action-conditioned noticeability metric for visual tokens or intermediate features, estimates a tolerance boundary or compression budget per token, and uses that budget for pruning, reuse, or feature compression. The main contribution appears more conceptual than architectural: safe compression should be defined by receiver behavior. The exact formulation, how action deviation thresholds are estimated, whether an auxiliary calibration model is used, and where compression is applied in the stack would need the full method section to verify.30:T9b2,方法分成理论拆解和算法设计两部分。

理论部分，作者先区分 mass coverage、output fidelity、task utility 三层目标。对 mass coverage，他们指出阈值计数 k(epsilon) 只是在问“有多少权重大于某阈值”，但压缩预算真正关心的是“要保留多少 token 才能覆盖 90% 之类的总概率质量”。决定后者的不是局部亮点，而是全局 score-gap profile，也就是排序后 logit 的衰减几何。论文给出一组 all-rank gap 条件：如果 gap envelope 在 log-rank 意义下斜率大于 1，tail 可求和，固定质量覆盖所需 budget 可以与长度无关；如果斜率低于 1，budget 会随长度增长。作者还用 Gaussian logits 说明一个反直觉点：即便看起来有“校准后的少量大权重”，要覆盖 90% mass 仍可能需要接近 0.61n 的 token，压缩空间并不大。

对 output fidelity，作者指出遗漏 mass 本身不是误差证书，关键在于被丢弃 value 的加权和是否能被恢复或近似。对一个固定 attention row，遗漏部分的 weighted sum 是精确的缺失统计量。进一步，如果希望一个线性 sketch 同时恢复完整输出和任意保留子预算下的输出，那么除了保留的真实 token 外，再加一个 tail aggregate 就达到匹配的维度下界。这给后面的算法设计提供了结构性依据：不是只保留 top-k token，而是要显式存一个 tail summary slot。

对 task utility，作者构造了 retrieval–aggregation 的 planted-token 模型，说明 exact attention 并不总是最适合任务目标。对 retrieval-like 任务，renormalized top-k 有时会因为压掉 diffuse noisy bulk 而优于 exact attention；但对 aggregation 任务，保留完整 softmax 更合理。也就是说，“更接近原 attention”不自动等于“更接近任务最优”。

基于这些分析，作者提出 CertKV。它是 training-free 的 KV compressor。设计上每个 head 预留一个 tail-summary slot，其余预算从 observation window 中选真实 token；分配策略不只看 attention score，还看 value dispersion，也就是尾部 value 是否容易被一个聚合向量概括。被省略的尾部用加权 key-value summary 存起来，且 synthetic slot 与真实 token 占用同样的物理预算。这个设计和很多只做 token selection 的方法不同，核心差异在于它承认“尾部不是纯噪声”，而是用一个显式统计量去补偿。31:T995,The paper has two layers: a theoretical decomposition and a practical compressor.

On mass coverage, the authors argue that threshold counts are the wrong primitive. Counting weights above epsilon does not answer the cache-budget question, which is how many tokens are needed to retain, say, 90% of the softmax mass. That quantity is governed by the global score-gap profile after sorting logits, not by a few bright entries. They derive complementary all-rank gap conditions: if the log-rank gap envelope has slope above one, the tail is summable and a fixed-mass budget can remain length-independent; if the slope is below one, the required budget grows with sequence length. A Gaussian-logit example makes the point concrete: one can observe a seemingly sparse calibrated count while still needing roughly 61% of tokens to retain 90% of the mass.

On output fidelity, the paper shows that omitted mass alone is not an error certificate. What matters is the weighted sum of omitted values. For a fixed realized attention row, that omitted weighted value sum is the exact missing statistic. Under a stronger linear-sketch requirement—recovering both the full output and every retained sub-budget—the authors show that keeping the selected values plus one tail aggregate achieves the matching dimension bound. This is the structural motivation for the algorithmic design: a compressor should not only keep top tokens, but also maintain an explicit tail summary.

On task utility, the paper introduces a planted retrieval–aggregation model. It shows that exact attention is not always the right target. For retrieval-like tasks, renormalized top-k can outperform exact attention by suppressing diffuse noisy mass, while for aggregation tasks exact attention remains preferable. So preserving the original attention output is not automatically the same as preserving task performance.

These analyses motivate CertKV, a training-free KV compressor. CertKV reserves one tail-summary slot per head, selects real tokens from an observation window, and allocates more token budget to heads whose omitted values are harder to summarize, measured through value dispersion. The omitted tail is stored as a weighted key-value summary, and the synthetic slot counts against the same physical budget as real tokens. This differs from pure token-selection methods by explicitly modeling the tail as compressed state rather than treating it as disposable noise.32:T4d5,The evaluation covers all 503 LongBench-v2 examples, three backbones, three compression ratios, multi-length RULER, one-factor studies, and a packed-cache prototype. The headline result is that under the pre-specified four-baseline comparison grid, CertKV is top-two in 7 of 9 LongBench-v2 settings. At 128K context on RULER it stays in the leading tier, and on Llama with 64K context and 10x compression it achieves the intended physical cache reduction.

The more useful part is how the experiments map onto the theory. One set of studies examines score-gap profiles versus mass coverage, showing that sparsity observed at shorter lengths does not reliably extrapolate to longer contexts. Another set tests the benefit of the tail summary for output fidelity, validating that the extra aggregate is not an ad hoc engineering trick but the exact statistic suggested by the analysis. A third controlled retrieval–aggregation setup recovers the predicted transition where renormalized top-k can beat exact attention for retrieval-like targets but not for aggregation. So the paper is not just reporting benchmark wins; it is checking whether the three separations—coverage, fidelity, and utility—actually explain empirical behavior.33:T927,技术路线分成两步。第一步，作者先研究一个理想化的 offline oracle：如果所有请求的完成长度事先已知，怎样分配到多个 replicas 才能最小化 step-level makespan。分析结论是，在长尾分布下，最优解呈现 tail-isolation-with-balancing 结构：把少量极长请求单独放到一个 tail replica 或 tail pool，其他大多数请求放到 bulk pool，但不是简单按请求数平均分，而是让两个池子的完成时间尽量平衡。作者进一步指出，一个简单的 top-k tail isolation 策略就能逼近大部分 oracle 收益，不必求解复杂的全局 assignment。

第二步，把这个结构在线化，形成 TailSieve。难点在于 rollout 前不知道哪些 prompt 会变成长尾，而且最优的 tail 大小和 replica 划分会随策略更新、长度分布变化、并发度变化而变化。作者利用一个经验事实：同一 prompt group 在相邻 rollout round 中，长度排序具有一定持续性。于是他们先做 partial rollout，在一个 cutoff 时刻观察哪些 prompt groups 仍未完成，把这些 unfinished groups 作为下一轮的高召回 tail 候选。这样得到的是 training-free tail signal，不需要额外训练长度预测器。

在此基础上，系统采用 two-pool routing：
1. bulk pool 处理大多数普通请求，保持较高并发；
2. tail pool 专门处理疑似长尾请求，使用较低并发，避免超长样本把大 batch decode 拖慢。

作者还设计了一个 hierarchical controller 联合调节两个量：tail isolation size 和 replica split。内层控制器根据观测到的完成时间平衡两个池子的结束时刻；外层控制器根据 response-work history 以及实测的 concurrency-throughput model，调节边际容量分配。这里的关键不是静态规则，而是随着 workload 演化在线跟踪最合适的隔离规模和资源占比。

论文特别强调两点边界。第一，它不同于 predictor-based skewness-aware dispatch，因为它不依赖额外长度模型。第二，它不同于异步或 partial-rollout reuse 系统，因为未完成轨迹不会跨 policy update 复用；下一轮只是重新生成这些 tail candidates。因此它保持 on-policy generation，不引入 routing-induced length bias，也不需要处理 policy lag。34:T990,The method has two layers. First, the authors analyze an offline oracle problem: if all completion lengths were known in advance, how should requests be assigned to replicas to minimize rollout-step makespan? Their main result is that, in the long-tail regime, the optimum has a tail-isolation-with-balancing structure. A small number of extreme-tail requests should be isolated onto a tail replica or tail pool, while the bulk of requests goes to a separate bulk pool. The goal is not to equalize request counts, but to balance completion times across pools. They further show that a simple top-k tail-isolation rule recovers most of the oracle gain, so the useful structure is much simpler than a full combinatorial assignment.

Second, they turn this structure into an online system called TailSieve. The challenge is that response lengths are unknown before generation, and the best tail size and replica split vary over time with policy updates, workload shifts, and concurrency-dependent decoding throughput. The key empirical observation is that prompt groups that are relatively long in one rollout round tend to remain relatively long in the next. TailSieve therefore runs a partial rollout, stops at a cutoff, and treats the unfinished prompt groups as high-recall tail candidates for the next round. This gives a training-free tail signal, avoiding an auxiliary length predictor.

The runtime then uses two-pool routing:
1. a bulk pool for most requests at higher concurrency;
2. a tail pool for likely long requests at lower concurrency, so a few very long generations do not stall large decoding batches.

A hierarchical controller jointly adapts two quantities: the tail isolation size and the replica split. The inner loop balances observed pool completion times, while the outer loop adjusts marginal capacity using response-work history and a measured concurrency-throughput model. The important point is that both workload assignment and hardware allocation are adapted online rather than fixed.

The paper is careful about what it does not do. It is not a predictor-based skewness-aware dispatcher, because it does not train a separate length model. It is also not an asynchronous or partial-rollout reuse system, because unfinished trajectories are not carried across policy updates. Tail candidates are regenerated from scratch under the current policy. That preserves on-policy sampling and avoids routing-induced length bias.35:T560,From the provided full-text excerpt, the experiments appear in three parts. First is the oracle analysis. The paper shows that, with known lengths, tail isolation with balancing beats uniform routing, and that a simple top-k isolation policy captures most of the oracle gain. Figure 2 is likely the key reference here because it justifies the structural claim rather than presenting a heuristic.

Second is the validation of the tail signal. The authors use unfinished prompt groups from a partial rollout as candidates for the next round, and Section 2.3 plus Appendix B and Figure 3 reportedly show that this signal has high recall. This is central to the method: if tail persistence across rounds were weak, the online approximation would fail.

Third is the end-to-end systems evaluation. TailSieve jointly controls tail workload and replica allocation as the rollout distribution evolves, and the paper claims lower step-level makespan while preserving on-policy generation. The excerpt does not include the full result tables, so exact gains, model sizes, GPU counts, or workload scales cannot be stated reliably. What is clear is that the relevant baselines include uniform routing, predictor-based skewness-aware dispatch, and asynchronous or partial-rollout-style alternatives, and that the main metric is rollout-step completion time rather than per-request latency.36:T40d,A good reading order is: theory first, online signal second, controller third. Start with Sections 2.1 and 2.2 to understand why the offline optimum has a tail-isolation-with-balancing form instead of simple load balancing by request count. That is the most informative part of the paper. Then read Section 2.3 and the figure on partial-rollout recall to see whether the tail signal is stable enough to support the online design. If your goal is to decide whether this is useful for an RL or OPD stack, focus on three items: the oracle figure, the tail-signal figure, and the main end-to-end table. For a deeper read, inspect two assumptions carefully: whether prompt-group persistence holds under more heterogeneous rollout workloads, and whether the concurrency-throughput model remains stable across different batch shapes, KV-cache pressure, and distributed settings.37:T520,WnW has two coordinated components: offline head triage and online chunk recall. In the offline stage, each KV head is scored along two axes. Voice score measures how strongly the head is grounded in audio rather than other modalities or generic sink behavior. Head sensitivity estimates how much quality is lost when that head’s KV cache is compressed, using a gradient-based sensitivity signal. Based on these two quantities, heads are partitioned into three roles. Anchor heads keep the full audio KV cache on GPU and act as decode-time observers of audio importance. Tidal heads keep only part of their audio KV on GPU while storing the complement on CPU, making those positions recallable. Fixed heads use a static prefill-time subset with no recall path. During decoding, attention from anchor heads is aggregated into chunk-level importance scores over the audio timeline. The highest-scoring chunks are recalled from CPU into the tidal heads’ GPU cache, while chunks that lose relevance are swapped out. The on-GPU cache therefore waxes and wanes with the generation process instead of shrinking monotonically. A key distinction from many text-side methods is that recall is driven by a small set of heads that preserve full temporal access to the audio, rather than by generic similarity heuristics.38:T421,The empirical story has two parts. First, the paper directly measures the mismatch between prefill and decode attention on LibriSpeech-Long with Voxtral. Prefill attention from the first generated token is concentrated near the start of the audio, whereas attention accumulated over the full decode is much more distributed. The top-K overlap between the two rankings is weak, which undermines the premise of prefill-only retention. Second, WnW delivers strong results under tight memory budgets. On two 3B backbones, Voxtral-mini-3b and Qwen2.5-Omni-3B, WnW stays within about 1.6 WER points of full-cache decoding even when only 20% of audio tokens remain on GPU. In the same regime, prefill-only baselines can fail to terminate and produce WER above 100%. The paper also reports generalization across languages, tasks, and domains, and favorable scaling behavior on a 24B backbone relative to other KV-management baselines. Importantly, the CPU-GPU recall overhead is reported to be limited, so the gains are not bought by an impractical runtime penalty.39:T9a8,论文先做了一个很关键的诊断实验：控制 drafter 可见的视觉预算，从无视觉、低预算到全视觉，观察 accept length 的变化。结论不是简单的“视觉越多越好”，而是最优预算随状态变化且明显非单调。作者把 preferred budget 定义为“达到最大 accept length 的最小预算”，而不是最高 token 概率或最低单步延迟。这个定义很合理，因为 speculative decoding 的核心目标是提高端到端吞吐，而 accept length 比局部概率更直接对应系统收益。实验里 25% 视觉预算在 56.0% 的状态上最优，而 full access 只在 2.9% 的状态上最优，说明固定全量视觉输入既浪费算力，也可能干扰草稿质量。

基于这个观察，作者提出 FOVEA。整体结构分三步。第一，先用 target model 的视觉编码器和 projector 对图像编码一次，得到 projected visual tokens，并构建每张图像的外部 visual memory。这样后续 draft 过程不需要反复处理整张图。第二，在 draft-tree 解码时，每个节点的 hidden state 作为 query 去检索这块 memory，选出与当前状态最相关的视觉证据，而且检索数量是动态的，不是固定 top-k。作者强调 dynamic cardinality，因为不同状态需要的证据量不同。第三，检索到的视觉证据不插入自回归 token 序列，而是通过一个 lightweight gated residual module 融合到当前节点的表示里，只影响当前 token scoring。这样做的关键好处是不会改变历史上下文，因此不会破坏已有 KV cache。

这里的方法取舍很清楚。若把检索到的视觉 token 真正拼回上下文，理论上表达能力更强，但历史 cache 会失效，推理加速收益会被重算吞掉。FOVEA 选择“外部记忆 + 当前状态修正”这条路，牺牲一部分深层交互，换取 cache reuse 和系统可实现性。对 speculative decoding 来说，这是合理的工程-算法折中。

从文中描述看，visual memory 至少包含用于检索的 key 表示和用于融合的 value/update 表示，先经 layer norm 和线性投影构建。每个 draft hidden state 对 memory 做相关性检索，得到 state-conditioned visual readout，再经门控残差注入当前表示。门控设计的意义在于：当当前 token 几乎不依赖视觉时，模型可以接近退化为纯文本 drafter；当需要视觉证据时，再有选择地放大视觉修正。3a:Ta86,The paper starts with a strong diagnostic. It varies the visual budget available to the drafter, from no visual input to full visual access, and measures accept length. The result is not monotonic: the preferred budget changes by state, and larger visual access is often suboptimal. The authors define preferred budget as the smallest tested budget that achieves the maximum accept length, rather than the budget with the highest token probability or lowest isolated latency. That choice is sensible because speculative decoding is ultimately about end-to-end throughput, and accept length is more directly tied to system gain. In their analysis, a 25% visual budget is optimal for 56.0% of evaluated states, while full access is optimal for only 2.9%, which already undermines the fixed-interface assumption.

Based on this observation, they propose FOVEA. The method has three main steps. First, the image is encoded once by the target-side visual encoder and multimodal projector, producing projected visual tokens that are stored in a reusable per-image visual memory. This avoids repeated full-image processing during drafting. Second, during draft-tree decoding, each draft hidden state acts as a query into that memory and retrieves the visual evidence most relevant to the current state. Importantly, retrieval cardinality is dynamic rather than fixed, because different states need different amounts of evidence. Third, the retrieved evidence is not inserted into the autoregressive token context. Instead, it is fused into the current node representation through a lightweight gated residual module, affecting only current-token scoring.

That design choice is the core systems insight. If the retrieved visual tokens were appended to the context, the historical KV cache would become inconsistent and would need recomputation, erasing much of the speculative speedup. FOVEA instead uses an external memory plus hidden-state correction, preserving cache reuse while still allowing state-conditioned visual adaptation. It is a deliberate trade-off: somewhat less expressive than rewriting the full context, but much more compatible with practical decoding.

From the method description, the visual memory contains at least retrieval-oriented key representations and fusion-oriented value/update representations, built from normalized projected visual tokens through learned projections. Each draft hidden state retrieves a state-conditioned visual readout, which is then injected via a gate. The gate matters because many decoding states are effectively text-dominant; in those cases the drafter should remain close to a text-only model, and only amplify visual correction when needed.3b:T5cb,Experiments span three vision-language backbones and nine multimodal benchmarks. The main outcomes are improved draft acceptance and improved end-to-end decoding speed relative to strong baselines, with up to 2.13× speedup over standard autoregressive decoding.

The diagnostic results are arguably even more informative than the headline speed number. Visual-budget sensitivity varies not only across tasks but also across generation stages within the same sample. The effect is especially pronounced on OCR-heavy tasks, where later tokens often need finer-grained visual evidence. This explains why static compressed visual interfaces can work in some phases and fail in others. The paper also shows that high visual budgets are rarely optimal: 75% and full access seldom win. That means excess visual context is not just computationally expensive; it can also hurt drafting quality by adding irrelevant evidence.

The full excerpt does not list every benchmark number, but the mechanism behind the gains is clear. FOVEA improves average accept length, reducing target-model fallback, while also avoiding repeated visual recomputation and cache invalidation. The most important ablations to inspect are likely fixed budget vs dynamic budget, context insertion vs gated residual fusion, with vs without external visual memory, and task-wise budget preference distributions. Those are the experiments that validate the paper’s central claim rather than merely reporting a speedup.3c:T418,For a quick pass, start with the visual-budget diagnostic in the introduction.
